question: What is the main muscle that makes you breathe in during normal quiet breathing?
explanation: The diaphragm is the primary muscle that pulls air into the lungs when it tightens and moves downward. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does air rush into your lungs when you take a breath in?

options.A: Abdominal muscles push air directly upward into the trachea
options.B: Intrapleural pressure drops below atmospheric pressure
options.C: Atmospheric pressure becomes lower than lung pressure
options.D: The chest wall actively squeezes air pockets open

explanation: Expanding the chest lowers the pressure inside the lungs compared to the outside air, making air flow inward. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which volume represents the normal amount of air inhaled or exhaled during quiet breathing?
explanation: Tidal volume is the standard amount of air moved in and out of the lungs with each normal, resting breath. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which lung volume can NEVER be measured directly using a standard handheld spirometer?
explanation: Residual volume stays inside the lungs even after blowing out as much air as possible, so it cannot be exhaled into a basic device. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which combination of volumes makes up the Vital Capacity?

options.A: Tidal volume and inspiratory reserve volume
options.C: Residual volume and expiratory reserve volume
options.D: Tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, and expiratory reserve volume

explanation: Vital capacity adds together all the volumes of air a person can actively move in and out of their lungs. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at term experiences a natural physiological reduction in which specific pulmonary capacity?
explanation: The growing uterus pushes the diaphragm up, which significantly decreases the air remaining in the lungs after a normal breath. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h3)

question: What body measurement is most closely linked to having larger lung volumes?
explanation: Taller individuals have larger chest cavities, which naturally hold more air than shorter frames. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why does lying flat on your back decrease the air left in your lungs after a normal breath?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure increases significantly at mattress level
options.B: The airways expand and lose their elastic recoil properties
options.C: Blood pools in the upper body and blocks air passages
options.D: Abdominal contents push the diaphragm upward into the chest

explanation: Gravity pulls the belly organs against the diaphragm when lying flat, which presses on the lungs and reduces resting air volume. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women more at risk for low blood oxygen levels when breathing becomes difficult?

options.A: The placenta absorbs all available oxygen before it reaches maternal lungs
options.B: They have increased oxygen demand combined with reduced functional residual capacity
options.C: Their red blood cells completely stop carrying oxygen during the third trimester
options.D: Their tidal volume drops to zero whenever they lie down flat

explanation: Higher body needs paired with a smaller air reserve mean pregnant women use up their oxygen stores faster. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following conditions is NOT typically associated with further compromising maternal lung capacities?
explanation: Mild exercise is a normal physiological state that does not damage chest wall mechanics or restrict lung capacity like pathological conditions do. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T3#BMP121_U1_T3_h5)
